name: logit
summary: The logit of a probability p is log(p/(1-p)), the inverse of the logistic sigmoid; in deep learning, the input of a sigmoid output unit, whose sigmoid gives a probability.

formula.v: logit(p) = σ⁻¹(p) = log(p / (1 − p)), for p in (0, 1)
formula.loc: Section 3.10, equation 3.38 and the sentence after it, p. 68

statistics.v: The inverse of the logistic sigmoid is called the logit in statistics; the book notes that the term for this function is rarely used in machine learning.

deep_learning.v: The variable z of a sigmoid output unit, whose sigmoid gives the probability of a binary outcome, is called a logit.

coined.v: Joseph Berkson, 1944, by analogy with the probit of Bliss

coined_in.v: Berkson, J. (1944). Application of the Logistic Function to Bio-Assay. Journal of the American Statistical Association 39(227), 357-365. doi:10.1080/01621459.1944.10500699
